answer: Each identity registers one shale slab as its test cell, locks an 80-credit bond, and fits an ivory collar with its serial. Each epoch the cell fires one timed pulse and files its decay log. An auditor recomputes the decay from the capacitance table for slab and collar; a missing log, reused trace, or mismatched collar burns the bond. The first test costs 36, the kth 36+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8028 and 1000 fakes cost 4,032,000 plus 80,000 bonded. A rented-cell ring fails because one serial cannot serve two keys. An honest agent pays 36 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
